mainTopic: Which foods are valid for the מצוה of מצה (טבל, מעשר שני, rich dough, ביכורים), and the rules on lukewarm water and soaking grain
overview: The amud opens by finishing the discussion of why טבל cannot be used for מצה. The גמרא concludes, as רב ששת said, that this follows רבי שמעון's rule אין איסור חל על איסור, after rejecting רבינא's attempt to fit it to the רבנן. Next, a ברייתא brings a dispute about לחם עוני. רבי יוסי הגלילי reads it as 'bread of a mourner' and excludes מעשר שני. רבי עקיבא reads it as 'poor bread' and excludes dough kneaded with wine, oil, or honey. The גמרא explains that the dispute turns on the spelling (עני) versus the pronunciation (עוני). It then resolves a story in which רבי עקיבא himself kneaded rich dough: the ban applies only to the first day's מצוה. A side discussion follows about why ordinary dough may not be kneaded with lukewarm water while מנחות may. The answer turns on the careful כהנים and the supervised place in the עזרה, and it also explains why the wheat of מנחות may not be soaked except for the communal עומר. Finally, a new ברייתא excludes ביכורים from the מצוה of מצה. רבי יוסי הגלילי learns this from 'in all your dwellings,' and רבי עקיבא learns it by comparing מצה to מרור. A challenge to רבי עקיבא's comparison continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Eating נבלה on יום הכפורים brings no extra liability
steps.stepSummary: This is the closing line of the ברייתא that shows רבי שמעון's view. Someone who eats נבלה on יום הכפורים is פטור from the יום הכפורים prohibition, because that איסור cannot take effect on food that is already forbidden.
steps.simpleTranslation: One who eats a נבלה on יום הכפורים is exempt.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing a quote from a ברייתא that shows רבי שמעון's rule: a new איסור cannot take effect on something that is already forbidden. This supports רב ששת's claim that our משנה follows רבי שמעון.
steps.deeperAnalysis: נבלה is already forbidden every day of the year. When יום הכפורים arrives, the extra איסור of eating on יום הכפורים does not take effect on it, so the eater is not liable for a קרבן חטאת for eating on יום הכפורים. In the same way, grain that was already טבל does not become forbidden as חמץ, and that is why it cannot count as 'something that could have been forbidden as חמץ' for the מצוה of מצה.

keyTerms.meaning: An animal that died without proper שחיטה; forbidden to eat
The fast day on which eating is forbidden
Exempt; here, not liable for the יום הכפורים prohibition
A prohibition does not take effect where another prohibition already exists (רבי שמעון's rule)

steps.confusionAlert: פטור here does not mean eating נבלה is allowed. The person still violated the איסור of נבלה. He is only exempt from the extra יום הכפורים prohibition, because it never took effect.

phrases.english: One who eats an animal carcass on Yom Kippur —
phrases.notes: Final clause of רבי שמעון's ברייתא, cited by רב ששת

phrases.english: is exempt.
phrases.notes: Exempt from the יום הכפורים prohibition, since it cannot take effect on food that is already forbidden

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the quote of רבי שמעון's ברייתא that רב ששת brought, earlier
steps.raayaObject: רב ששת's claim that the exclusion of טבל follows רבי שמעון
steps.raayaSupportSource: רבי שמעון's ברייתא: נבלה eaten on יום הכפורים brings no liability for יום הכפורים
steps.whyThisMatters: This case shows clearly how אין איסור חל על איסור works, and that same principle explains why טבל fails for מצה.

steps.title: רבינא explains the rule even according to the רבנן
steps.stepSummary: רבינא says we do not need רבי שמעון. Even the רבנן, who hold that one איסור can take effect on another, would exclude טבל. The verse refers to food whose איסור comes only from חמץ, and טבל is forbidden for a second reason as well.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבינא said: you can even say the ruling follows the רבנן. The מצה must be something whose prohibition, if it became חמץ, would be only 'do not eat חמץ'. This excludes טבל, whose prohibition is not only 'do not eat חמץ' but also 'do not eat טבל'.
steps.whatsHappening: רבינא offers a different way to explain why טבל cannot be used for מצה, one that also works for the רבנן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב ששת needed רבי שמעון's rule to say the חמץ prohibition never takes effect on טבל. רבינא accepts that it might take effect, as the רבנן hold. He argues instead that the verse requires the food to have the חמץ איסור by itself, with no other איסור added. Because טבל carries two prohibitions, it does not qualify.

keyTerms.meaning: An אמורא who offers an alternative explanation
You can even say it follows the Rabbis
The prohibition: do not eat leavened bread
Only; exclusively
Produce from which תרומות and מעשרות have not yet been separated; forbidden to eat

phrases.english: Ravina said: You can even say it follows the Rabbis:

phrases.aramaic: מִי שֶׁאִיסּוּרוֹ מִשּׁוּם ״בַּל תֹּאכַל חָמֵץ״ בִּלְבַד.
phrases.english: Matza must be from something whose prohibition is due only to 'do not eat leavened bread.'
This excludes this one, whose prohibition is not
due only to 'do not eat leavened bread,'
but also due to 'do not eat untithed produce.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers an alternative to רב ששת's dependence on רבי שמעון
steps.terutzHavaAmina: It seemed that excluding טבל required רבי שמעון's rule that one איסור cannot take effect on another
steps.terutzMaskana: The criterion is food forbidden only by חמץ; טבל has an extra איסור, so it is excluded even according to the רבנן

steps.title: The word 'only' is not written
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects רבינא's explanation. The source never says בלבד, so there is no basis for requiring that the חמץ איסור be the only one.
steps.simpleTranslation: Is the word 'only' written?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks רבינא's explanation with a short question.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבינא's whole explanation rests on the word 'only'. The source requires only something that can become forbidden as חמץ. It does not demand that חמץ be the sole איסור, so רבינא added a condition that is not in the text.

keyTerms.meaning: Is it written? (rhetorical: it is not written)

phrases.english: Is 'only' written?
phrases.notes: A rhetorical question that functions as a rejection

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects רבינא's alternative
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: It depends on the word בלבד, which does not appear in the source

steps.title: Conclusion: רב ששת's explanation stands
steps.stepSummary: Since רבינא's approach fails, the גמרא concludes that the exclusion of טבל is best explained as רב ששת said, following רבי שמעון.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, it is clear that the explanation is as רב ששת said.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא closes the discussion and returns to רב ששת's explanation.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Once 'only' is shown not to be written, the remaining way to exclude טבל is רבי שמעון's rule. The חמץ איסור never takes effect on טבל, so טבל is not 'something that becomes forbidden as חמץ'.

keyTerms.meaning: It is clear; the clear conclusion is
The אמורא who attributed the ruling to רבי שמעון

steps.whatToRemember: The משנה's exclusion of טבל from מצה follows רבי שמעון's rule אין איסור חל על איסור. רבינא's attempt to fit it to the רבנן was rejected because the word בלבד is not written.

phrases.english: Rather, it is clear: it is as Rav Sheshet explained.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Follows from the rejection of רבינא
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The exclusion of טבל follows רבי שמעון, as רב ששת said

steps.title: מעשר שני cannot be used for מצה: לחם עוני
steps.stepSummary: A new ברייתא. רבי יוסי הגלילי derives from לחם עוני that מצה must be food an אונן may eat. מעשר שני, which may be eaten only in joy and not during אנינות, is therefore excluded.
steps.simpleTranslation: The רבנן taught: I might have thought a person fulfills his obligation of מצה with מעשר שני in ירושלים. The verse says 'לחם עוני': it must be something eaten during אנינות. This excludes מעשר שני, which is not eaten during אנינות but only in joy. These are the words of רבי יוסי הגלילי.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins a new topic. It brings a ברייתא that asks whether מעשר שני can be used for the מצוה of מצה, and it answers no, based on a verse.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word עוני is read as if it hinted at אונן, a mourner on the day a close relative died. The Torah forbids an אונן to eat מעשר שני, which must be eaten in a state of שמחה. So the verse is read to require מצה that even an אונן could eat, and מעשר שני fails that test.

keyTerms.meaning: Second tithe; produce eaten in ירושלים
Bread of affliction (דברים טז:ג)
The state of acute mourning on the day of a close relative's death
Joy; the state required for eating מעשר שני
The תנא who gives this derivation
I might have thought... therefore the verse says

steps.confusionAlert: עוני is spelled with an ע (poverty), not with an א (mourning). The derivation is a wordplay connecting the two. It is not the plain meaning of the word.
steps.whyThisMatters: This opens a new discussion about which kinds of sanctified produce can fulfill the מצוה of מצה. The view is attributed to רבי יוסי הגלילי, which hints that others may disagree.

phrases.english: The Rabbis taught:
I might have thought a person fulfills his obligation
with second tithe in Jerusalem,
therefore the verse says: 'bread of affliction,'
meaning something that may be eaten during acute mourning.
phrases.notes: עוני is read as hinting at אונן

phrases.english: This excludes this, which is not eaten during acute mourning,
but only in joy —
these are the words of Rabbi Yosei HaGelili.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: יָכוֹל יוֹצֵא אָדָם יְדֵי חוֹבָתוֹ בְּמַעֲשֵׂר שֵׁנִי בִּירוּשָׁלַיִם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins a new topic: whether מעשר שני can be used for מצה
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רבי יוסי הגלילי, one does not fulfill the מצוה of מצה with מעשר שני, because מצה must be food that may be eaten during אנינות

steps.title: רבי עקיבא: the extra word מצות widens, and לחם עוני excludes rich dough
steps.stepSummary: רבי עקיבא learns from the repeated word מצות that many kinds of מצה are valid. He uses לחם עוני to exclude dough kneaded with wine, oil, or honey.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי עקיבא says: the Torah repeats the word 'מצות,' which comes to include more. If so, why does the verse say 'לחם עוני'? To exclude dough kneaded with wine, oil, or honey.
steps.whatsHappening: The same ברייתא now brings a second opinion. רבי עקיבא gives his own reading of the verses about מצה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since the word מצות appears again and again, רבי עקיבא treats the extra mentions as a רִיבּוּי, a widening that includes all kinds of מצה. That leaves the phrase לחם עוני free to teach a limit. He reads it as 'poor bread,' so rich dough made with wine, oil, or honey does not qualify. This is a different use of לחם עוני from רבי יוסי הגלילי's in Step 5, where it excluded מעשר שני.

keyTerms.meaning: included / widened (a repeated word teaches something extra)
Why does the verse say this? (what does this extra phrase come to teach?)
to exclude; except for
dough that was kneaded

phrases.english: Rabbi Akiva says:
'Matzot,' 'matzot' (the repeated word) comes to include more.
phrases.notes: The word מצות appears several times in the Torah's verses about Pesach.

phrases.aramaic: אִם כֵּן, מָה תַּלְמוּד לוֹמַר ״לֶחֶם עוֹנִי״?
phrases.english: If so, what does the verse teach by saying 'lechem oni'?
To exclude dough that was kneaded
with wine, oil, or honey.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a second opinion in the same ברייתא, reading לחם עוני differently from רבי יוסי הגלילי.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: מצה kneaded with wine, oil, or honey is not valid לחם עוני. Otherwise, all kinds of מצה are included.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is the source for the idea that the מצה of the מצוה must be 'poor' and not rich dough (מצה עשירה).

steps.title: Asking for the reason behind רבי עקיבא's reading
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why רבי עקיבא understands לחם עוני as 'poor bread.'
steps.simpleTranslation: What is רבי עקיבא's reason?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a short question to set up the next step: why does רבי עקיבא read the phrase as 'poor bread' and not as 'bread of a mourner'?
steps.deeperAnalysis: The same words, לחם עוני, led רבי יוסי הגלילי to a rule about an אונן, a mourner. The גמרא wants to know what in the verse pushes רבי עקיבא to read it as 'poor' instead.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the reason?

phrases.english: What is the reason of Rabbi Akiva?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the textual basis of the reading given in Step 6.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What in the verse leads רבי עקיבא to read לחם עוני as 'poor bread'?

steps.title: The word is spelled עני, meaning poor
steps.stepSummary: The written spelling (כתיב) is עני, without a vav. That spelling means 'poor,' not 'mourning.'
steps.simpleTranslation: Is it written 'עוני' (with a vav)? It is written 'עני' (without a vav).
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that רבי עקיבא goes by how the word is spelled in the Torah scroll.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the Torah the word is written ע־נ־י, with no vav. That spelling naturally reads עָנִי, 'poor.' So רבי עקיבא learns that the מצה must be poor bread, made only of flour and water.

keyTerms.meaning: it is written (how the word is spelled in the Torah)
a poor person; poor

steps.confusionAlert: Some words in the Torah are spelled one way (כתיב) but read aloud another way (קרי). Here the spelling is עני and the reading is עוני. The argument in the next steps depends on this difference.

phrases.english: Is it written 'lechem oni' (with a vav)?
It is written 'ani' (without a vav, meaning poor).

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of Step 7.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: רבי עקיבא follows the spelling (כתיב), עני, which means poor.

steps.title: רבי יוסי הגלילי: we pronounce it עוני
steps.stepSummary: From רבי יוסי הגלילי's side: the word is read aloud (קרי) as עוני, which points to mourning.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי יוסי הגלילי: do we read it 'ani'? We read it 'oni'!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא presents רבי יוסי הגלילי's response. Our tradition pronounces the word עוני, so the 'mourner' meaning should count.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי עקיבא relies on the spelling, while רבי יוסי הגלילי relies on the pronunciation. The pronunciation עוני sounds like אונן, a mourner. That supports his rule that מצה must be food a mourner may eat, which excludes מעשר שני.

keyTerms.meaning: we read / pronounce it (the קרי)
affliction or mourning (the pronounced form)

phrases.english: And Rabbi Yosei HaGelili (would say):
Do we read it 'ani'?!
We read it 'oni.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Pushes back on Step 8 by pointing to the pronunciation instead of the spelling.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי עקיבא's reliance on the spelling עני
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The traditional pronunciation is עוני, which points to mourning rather than poverty.

steps.title: רבי עקיבא explains the pronunciation through שמואל
steps.stepSummary: רבי עקיבא says the pronunciation עוני teaches something else: it is bread over which many words are said (עונין).
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי עקיבא: the fact that we read it 'oni' follows שמואל. As שמואל said: 'לחם עוני' means bread over which many things are said.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי עקיבא answers. The pronunciation עוני is not about mourners. It teaches שמואל's idea that we say many words over the מצה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The reading עוני is linked to the word עונין, meaning 'answering' or 'reciting,' as in saying the הגדה over the מצה. Since the pronunciation teaches that lesson, it does not undo the spelling's lesson. רבי עקיבא can keep his rule that the מצה must be 'poor bread.'

keyTerms.meaning: in line with שמואל's teaching
that people recite / answer over it
many words (the הגדה)

steps.whatToRemember: Both readings are used. The spelling עני (poor) gives רבי עקיבא's rule against rich dough. The pronunciation עוני gives שמואל's teaching that we recite the הגדה over the מצה.

phrases.english: And Rabbi Akiva (would say):
The fact that we read it 'oni'
is in line with Shmuel. As Shmuel said:
'Lechem oni' means
bread over which many things are recited.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers Step 9's objection.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Gives the pronunciation a different lesson, so the spelling's lesson still stands.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The pronunciation עוני seems to point to mourning, which would weaken רבי עקיבא's reading.
steps.terutzMaskana: The pronunciation teaches שמואל's idea of reciting over the מצה, and the spelling still teaches 'poor bread.'
steps.whyThisMatters: שמואל's teaching is the basis for saying the הגדה over the מצה at the סדר.

steps.title: Challenge: רבי עקיבא himself kneaded dough with wine, oil, and honey
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא records that רבי עקיבא kneaded dough with wine, oil, and honey for רבי אליעזר and רבי יהושע, and they did not object. This seems to contradict his own rule.
steps.simpleTranslation: Does רבי עקיבא really hold that dough kneaded with wine, oil, and honey may not be used? But a ברייתא teaches: one may not knead dough on פסח with wine, oil, or honey. If one did, רבן גמליאל says it must be burned at once, and the חכמים say it may be eaten. And רבי עקיבא said: it was my week to serve רבי אליעזר and רבי יהושע, and I kneaded dough for them with wine, oil, and honey, and they said nothing to me.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רבי עקיבא's rule from Step 6. It quotes a story in which he made exactly that kind of dough for great Rabbis on פסח, and nobody objected. The answer comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In Step 6, רבי עקיבא excludes dough kneaded with wine, oil, or honey. In this ברייתא, he kneads such dough himself and his teachers approve by staying silent, which suggests it is acceptable. The ברייתא also brings a dispute about rich dough: רבן גמליאל says to burn it immediately because it becomes חמץ quickly, and the חכמים allow eating it.

keyTerms.meaning: But it was taught in a ברייתא (introduces a contradicting source)
one may not knead
it must be burned immediately
it may be eaten
my turn / my week of service
and they said nothing to me (silent approval)

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up the two questions. One is whether rich dough is permitted to eat on פסח (the dispute between רבן גמליאל and the חכמים). The other is whether it counts as the מצוה of מצה (רבי עקיבא's rule in Step 6). The answer will turn on keeping these apart.

phrases.english: And does Rabbi Akiva hold

phrases.aramaic: עִיסָּה שֶׁנִּילּוֹשָׁה בְּיַיִן וְשֶׁמֶן וּדְבַשׁ לָא?
phrases.english: that dough kneaded with wine, oil, or honey is not (valid)?
But it was taught: one may not knead dough on Pesach
with wine, oil, or honey.
And if one kneaded (it),
Rabban Gamliel says: it must be burned immediately,
and the Sages say: it may be eaten.
And Rabbi Akiva said:
It was my turn of service with
Rabbi Eliezer and Rabbi Yehoshua,
and I kneaded dough for them
with wine, oil, and honey,
and they said nothing to me.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְסָבַר רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא עִיסָּה שֶׁנִּילּוֹשָׁה בְּיַיִן וְשֶׁמֶן וּדְבַשׁ לָא? וְהָתַנְיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Goes back to רבי עקיבא's rule from Step 6 and challenges it with a contradicting ברייתא.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי עקיבא's rule that dough kneaded with wine, oil, or honey is excluded
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבי עקיבא himself kneaded such dough on פסח, and רבי אליעזר and רבי יהושע did not object. This implies such dough is acceptable.

steps.title: The ברייתא continues: spreading on dough, the view of the חכמים, and warm water
steps.stepSummary: The rest of the ברייתא is quoted. It discusses spreading wine, oil, or honey on top of the dough, gives the view of the חכמים, and ends with a point everyone agrees on: no kneading with warm water. This completes the challenge against רבי עקיבא.
steps.simpleTranslation: The ברייתא continues: 'Even though one may not knead dough with these liquids, one may spread them on its surface.' (The גמרא notes: this part follows the תנא קמא.) 'The חכמים say: whatever you may knead with, you may also spread on top. Whatever you may not knead with, you may not spread on top either. And everyone agrees that one may not knead the dough with lukewarm water.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing the quote of the ברייתא it started in step 11. The full text shows clearly that רבי עקיבא really did make dough with wine, oil, and honey on פסח.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The line 'even though one may not knead' matches the תנא קמא, who forbids kneading with these liquids. The גמרא adds a short side note to point that out. The חכמים link the two acts: spreading is allowed only where kneading is allowed. Everyone agrees that warm water is forbidden, because it makes dough rise into חמץ quickly. The challenge itself stays the same: רבי עקיבא's own actions seem to clash with his rule from earlier.

keyTerms.meaning: spread or smear a liquid on the surface of the dough
we have come back to the view of the first anonymous opinion
and all agree
lukewarm water

steps.confusionAlert: This is not a new topic. It is the second half of the ברייתא from step 11. The challenge against רבי עקיבא is still the main point.

phrases.english: And even though one may not knead [with them],
phrases.notes: Still part of the ברייתא's wording.

phrases.english: one may spread [them] on it (the dough's surface)
[The גמרא comments:] we have come back to the first tanna.
phrases.notes: A short side note from the גמרא in the middle of the quote.

phrases.english: And the Rabbis say:
With what one may knead, one may spread.
And with what one may not knead,
one may not spread.
And all agree that one may not knead
the dough with lukewarm water!
phrases.notes: Warm water speeds up rising, so it risks חמץ.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאַף עַל פִּי שֶׁאֵין לָשִׁין, מְקַטְּפִין בּוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the ברייתא quoted as a challenge in step 11.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי עקיבא's rule that מצה made with wine, oil, or honey does not count as לחם עוני
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא shows רבי עקיבא himself kneading מצה with these liquids, and the great teachers did not object.

steps.title: First day versus second day
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that רבי עקיבא's rule is for the first day of יום טוב. The dough he kneaded was for the second day.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is not difficult. This rule (rich מצה does not count) is about the first day of יום טוב. That story (he kneaded with wine, oil, and honey) is about the second day.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא resolves the contradiction by saying the two sources speak about different days of פסח.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Only on the first night is there a מצוה to eat מצה, and that מצה must be real לחם עוני. On the other days, the only rule is not to eat חמץ. So enriched מצה is fine to eat then. רבי עקיבא's rule and his actions do not clash.

keyTerms.meaning: it is not difficult; the standard opening of an answer
the first day of the festival, when eating מצה is a מצוה
the second day, and the days after, when there is no special מצוה of מצה

steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that the rules of לחם עוני matter only for the מצוה of eating מצה on the first night. They do not apply to every piece of מצה eaten during פסח.

phrases.english: It is not difficult:
this is on the first day of the festival,
that is on the second day of the festival.

steps.triggerLanguage: לָא קַשְׁיָא: הָא בְּיוֹם טוֹב רִאשׁוֹן. הָא בְּיוֹם טוֹב שֵׁנִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge from the ברייתא in steps 11-12.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting the cases: different days of פסח
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי עקיבא's rule seemed to ban rich מצה for all of פסח, so his own kneading seemed to contradict it.
steps.terutzMaskana: The rule covers only the first-night מצוה. On later days, rich מצה is allowed.

steps.title: רבי יהושע's instruction to his sons
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא supports the first-day/later-day split with רבי יהושע's words: on the first day, don't knead my dough with milk; after that, do.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is like what רבי יהושע said to his sons: 'On the first day, do not knead dough for me with milk. From then on, knead it for me with milk.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a story that seems to show the same idea: enriched dough is avoided on the first day and allowed afterward.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהושע treats the first day differently from the later days. That fits the answer in step 13 exactly. The milk detail, though, will cause a problem in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: the first day
milk
from here onward; afterward

phrases.english: As Rabbi Yehoshua said to his sons:

phrases.english: On the first day, do not knead [dough] for me with milk;
from then on, knead [it] for me with milk.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings support for the answer in step 13.

steps.title: But milk dough is forbidden all year
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the story: a ברייתא says dough may never be kneaded with milk. If it is, the whole bread is forbidden, because people may come to eat it with meat.
steps.simpleTranslation: But it was taught in a ברייתא: one may not knead dough with milk. If he did, all the bread is forbidden, because it can lead a person into sin.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא questions the story about רבי יהושע. How could he ask for milk dough at all, when milk bread is forbidden?
steps.deeperAnalysis: Milk bread looks like ordinary bread. Someone might forget and eat it with meat, which is בשר בחלב. So חז"ל forbade it all year. This seems to contradict רבי יהושע's request.

keyTerms.meaning: but it was taught in a ברייתא; it opens a challenge from a source
bread
getting used to sin; a habit that leads to a violation

phrases.english: But wasn't it taught:
one may not knead dough with milk,
and if he kneaded, the entire bread is forbidden,
because of becoming accustomed to sin.
phrases.notes: He may come to eat it with meat.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָתַנְיָא: אֵין לָשִׁין אֶת הָעִיסָּה בְּחָלָב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the supporting story from step 14.
steps.kashyaTarget: The story that רבי יהושע asked for dough kneaded with milk
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A ברייתא forbids milk dough completely, so רבי יהושע would not have asked for it.

steps.title: He meant honey, not milk
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rereads רבי יהושע's words: he really said honey.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, this is what he said: 'On the first day, do not knead dough for me with honey. From then on, knead it for me with honey.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the problem by changing the ingredient in the story from milk to honey.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Honey dough raises no meat-and-milk worry. It is still 'rich' dough, so the story still supports the first-day/later-day split. The proof stays strong, and the problem from step 15 goes away.

honey

phrases.english: On the first day, do not knead [dough] for me with honey;
from then on, knead [it] for me with honey.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in step 15.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Rereading the wording of the story
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי יהושע asked for milk dough, which is forbidden.
steps.terutzMaskana: He asked for honey dough, which is permitted and is still enriched dough.

steps.title: Or it really was milk, shaped like an ox's eye
steps.stepSummary: A second answer: the dough really was made with milk, but it was shaped in a special way, like an ox's eye. רבינא rules that this is permitted.
steps.simpleTranslation: Or, if you prefer, say: it really was with milk. As רבינא said: if it is made shaped like an ox's eye, it is permitted. Here too, it was shaped like an ox's eye.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives another way to answer the problem. It keeps the word 'milk' and explains why that milk dough was allowed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Milk bread is forbidden only because it looks like regular bread. If it has an unusual shape, everyone will know it is milky. Then no one will eat it with meat by mistake. So רבי יהושע could ask for milk dough as long as it had a special shape.

keyTerms.meaning: and if you wish, say; it introduces a second answer
really; in truth (keeping the original reading)
like the eye of an ox; a special, recognizable shape
it is permitted

steps.whatToRemember: רבי עקיבא's ban on rich מצה applies only to the first night's מצוה. On later days it is fine. In the story of רבי יהושע, the dough was either made with honey, or made with milk in a special shape (כעין תורא) so no one would eat it with meat.

[if shaped] like an ox's eye, it is permitted.

steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the ban to ordinary-looking bread
steps.terutzHavaAmina: All milk bread is forbidden, so רבי יהושע could not have asked for it.
steps.terutzMaskana: Milk bread with a special shape is permitted, because no one will mistake it and eat it with meat.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The first-day/later-day split stands. Rich מצה is allowed after the first night.

steps.title: Everyone agrees: no kneading dough with lukewarm water
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes a line from the earlier ברייתא: all opinions agree that dough may not be kneaded with פושרין (lukewarm water).
steps.simpleTranslation: And everyone agrees that one may not knead dough with lukewarm water.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back and picks up one line from the ברייתא it discussed earlier. This line is the starting point for a new discussion.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Lukewarm water makes dough rise and become חמץ much faster. So even the opinions that argued about other liquids agree that you may not use פושרין for dough on פסח.

keyTerms.meaning: And they agree (all opinions in the dispute)

steps.triggerLanguage: וְשָׁוִין שֶׁאֵין לָשִׁין אֶת הָעִיסָּה בְּפוֹשְׁרִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the milk-dough discussion and returns to another line of the earlier ברייתא as a new topic.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: No one may knead dough for פסח with lukewarm water.

steps.title: But meal-offerings are kneaded with lukewarm water
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the rule: a משנה says all מנחות are kneaded with פושרין and watched so they do not become חמץ.
steps.simpleTranslation: How is this different from meal-offerings? We learned in a משנה: all meal-offerings are kneaded with lukewarm water, and they are watched so they do not become חמץ.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא points to a contradiction. In the בית המקדש, מנחות are kneaded with lukewarm water, so why is regular dough not allowed?
steps.deeperAnalysis: מנחות also must not become חמץ. If careful watching is enough there, why not let everyone use lukewarm water and simply watch the dough?

keyTerms.meaning: What is the difference?
Flour offerings brought in the בית המקדש

They are watched carefully

steps.kashyaTarget: The ban on kneading dough with פושרין
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The משנה allows פושרין for מנחות as long as they are watched. That suggests watching is enough, so the ban seems unnecessary.

steps.title: The כהנים are careful; ordinary people are not
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the lenient rule was given for the careful כהנים. It cannot be applied to ordinary people who are not as careful.
steps.simpleTranslation: If they said it for careful people, should they say it for people who are not careful?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the difference. כהנים are careful and can be trusted to watch the dough, but regular people cannot.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The two rules do not contradict each other. Lukewarm water is risky, and only experts who watch closely can handle that risk. Ordinary people get the stricter rule.

keyTerms.meaning: Careful, quick, diligent people (the כהנים)
If they said (if the Rabbis allowed)

steps.whatToRemember: פושרין is allowed for מנחות only because the כהנים are זריזין.

phrases.english: If they said it about the careful ones,

steps.triggerLanguage: אִם אָמְרוּ בִּזְרִיזִין יֹאמְרוּ בְּשֶׁאֵין זְרִיזִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge from מנחות.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: If watching works for מנחות, it should work for everyone.
steps.terutzMaskana: Watching is only reliable when careful כהנים do it.

steps.title: Then why can't the כהנים soak the wheat?
steps.stepSummary: If careful כהנים can be trusted, the wheat of מנחות should also be soaked. Yet שמואל rules that it may not be soaked.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, let them also soak the wheat! Why then did רבי זירא say, in the name of רבה בר ירמיה in the name of שמואל: the wheat of meal-offerings may not be soaked?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the last answer. If the כהנים are careful enough for lukewarm water, they should be careful enough to soak the wheat too.
steps.deeperAnalysis: לתיתה means soaking wheat in water to loosen the husks before grinding, and it carries a risk of חמץ. If being careful is enough, שמואל's ban on soaking מנחות wheat seems unnecessary.

phrases.english: wheat of meal-offerings, one does not soak it!

steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Carefulness should also permit soaking, but שמואל forbids soaking מנחות wheat.

steps.title: Kneading is done by careful people; soaking is not
steps.stepSummary: Kneading מנחות is done by the careful כהנים, but soaking the wheat is not done by them.
steps.simpleTranslation: Kneading is done by the careful ones; soaking is not done by the careful ones.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the two jobs are done by different people. Careful כהנים knead, but the soaking happens earlier and is done by others.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The heter for lukewarm water depends on who does the work. Since soaking is done by people who are not זריזין, the carefulness reason does not apply, so soaking is forbidden.

keyTerms.meaning: Kneading
It is (it exists, it is done)

steps.terutzMaskana: Only kneading is done by זריזין, not soaking.

steps.title: But kneading can be done by anyone, even a non-כהן
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the claim that kneading is done by careful כהנים. The פסוק shows that only from קמיצה onward must a כהן act, so pouring and mixing are valid by anyone.
steps.simpleTranslation: Is kneading really done by the careful ones? But the פסוק says: 'And he shall pour oil on it, etc., and bring it to the כהן.' From the scooping onward it is the job of the כהנים. This teaches that pouring and mixing are valid by any person!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the last answer. A דרשה shows that the mixing of a מנחה does not need a כהן, so kneading is not necessarily done by careful people.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the פסוק, pouring oil comes before 'bring it to the כהן.' So the כהן's role begins only at קמיצה, and earlier steps like יציקה and בלילה may be done by a non-כהן. If kneading is not done by זריזין, the earlier answer falls apart.

keyTerms.meaning: But it is written (a פסוק that challenges)

steps.title: Kneading happens in the place of the careful ones
steps.stepSummary: Even if a non-כהן may knead, the kneading still happens in the עזרה, where the careful כהנים are.
steps.simpleTranslation: Kneading: granted it is not done by the careful ones, it is done in the place of the careful ones.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא adjusts its answer. It admits a non-כהן may knead, but says the kneading takes place in the עזרה, under the eyes of the careful כהנים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The protection now comes from the place, not from the person. Because the kneading happens where the זריזין are, it is supervised well enough to allow lukewarm water.

steps.terutzMaskana: Kneading is protected because it happens in the עזרה, the place of the careful ones.

steps.title: Proof: mixing outside the courtyard is invalid
steps.stepSummary: A teaching says בלילה is valid by a זר, but if it is done outside the wall of the עזרה, the מנחה is invalid.
steps.simpleTranslation: As the Master said: mixing is valid by a non-כהן, but if it is done outside the wall of the courtyard, it is invalid.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a source to prove that kneading must take place in the עזרה, even when a non-כהן does it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This teaching has two parts. Anyone may mix, but only inside the עזרה. That is exactly the claim of the previous answer: kneading is not tied to the person, but it is tied to the place.

steps.title: Soaking has neither careful people nor a careful place
steps.stepSummary: The rule excludes לתיתה, which is done neither by careful people nor in the careful place, so soaking מנחות wheat stays forbidden.
steps.simpleTranslation: This excludes soaking, which is done neither by the careful ones nor in the place of the careful ones.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא wraps up the discussion. It explains why kneading with lukewarm water is allowed for מנחות, while soaking the wheat is not.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Kneading has at least one safeguard: it happens in the עזרה. Soaking has no safeguard at all, since it is not done by כהנים or in the עזרה. So שמואל's ban on soaking makes sense.

keyTerms.meaning: To exclude

steps.whyThisMatters: This explains the rule that ordinary people may not use פושרין on פסח. A risky step is allowed only where there is strong supervision, either careful people or a careful place.

phrases.english: To exclude soaking,

steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Kneading מנחות with פושרין is allowed because it happens in the עזרה. Soaking the wheat is forbidden because it has neither careful people nor a careful place.

steps.title: Challenge from the soaking of the עומר offering
steps.stepSummary: If soaking grain risks חמץ, why is the מנחת העומר soaked?

steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges שמואל's rule that the wheat of מנחות may not be soaked. It points to the מנחת העומר, which is also a meal-offering, and which a ברייתא says is soaked and piled up. The next step answers this.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 26 concluded that לתיתה is forbidden when the work is done neither by careful people nor in a careful place. The עומר also must never become חמץ, yet its grain is soaked. That looks like a contradiction to the rule.

steps.title: A community offering is different
steps.stepSummary: The עומר is a communal act and is handled with extra care.
steps.simpleTranslation: The community is different.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the עומר is different because it is a community (ציבור) offering.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Work done for the whole community is supervised by the בית דין, and the people doing it are very careful. So the risk of חמץ does not apply there. Ordinary מנחות have no such supervision at the soaking stage, so soaking their wheat stays forbidden, as שמואל ruled.

keyTerms.meaning: The community; a public or communal act

steps.whatToRemember: The wheat of מנחות may not be soaked, because the soaking is not done by careful people or in a careful place. The מנחת העומר is an exception only because a community act is done with great care.

phrases.english: The community is different.
phrases.notes: A communal act is closely supervised, so it is done carefully.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the עומר challenge
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinguishes the cases (communal care versus private)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Soaking the עומר shows that soaking is generally safe

steps.title: מצה from ביכורים does not count, according to רבי יוסי הגלילי
steps.stepSummary: The verse 'in all your dwellings' excludes ביכורים, which may be eaten only in ירושלים.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Rabbis taught: Could a person fulfill his obligation with ביכורים? The verse says, 'In all your dwellings you shall eat מצות.' This means מצה that may be eaten in all your dwellings. That excludes ביכורים, which may not be eaten everywhere but only in ירושלים. These are the words of רבי יוסי הגלילי.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new topic with a ברייתא. It asks whether מצה made from ביכורים wheat counts for the מצוה, and רבי יוסי הגלילי says it does not.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The verse requires מצה that is fit to be eaten 'in all your dwellings,' meaning anywhere. ביכורים may be eaten only in ירושלים, so they fail this test. The source for the rule is the wording of the verse.

keyTerms.meaning: First fruits brought to the בית המקדש and eaten only in ירושלים
His obligation (fulfilling the מצוה)

steps.confusionAlert: Wheat is one of the seven species brought as ביכורים. So the question is about real wheat מצה, not about a strange grain.

steps.mimraCoreRuling: One cannot fulfill the מצוה of מצה with ביכורים, because they may not be eaten everywhere.

steps.title: רבי עקיבא learns the rule by comparing מצה to מרור
steps.stepSummary: Just as מרור is not ביכורים, מצה also may not be ביכורים.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי עקיבא says: מצה and מרור are compared. Just as מרור is not ביכורים, so too מצה must not be ביכורים.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי עקיבא agrees with the ruling but gives a different source for it. He compares מצה to מרור, since the Torah mentions them together.
steps.deeperAnalysis: מרור never comes from ביכורים. By linking the two מצוות, רבי עקיבא says מצה also may not be ביכורים. The ruling stays the same as in Step 29; only the source changes.

keyTerms.meaning: Bitter herbs eaten at the סדר
Just as ... so too (a comparison formula)

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a different source for the same ruling
steps.mimraCoreRuling: מצה from ביכורים is invalid, learned by comparison to מרור.

steps.title: Perhaps the comparison excludes the whole species
steps.stepSummary: Maybe the comparison means that מצה must come from a grain species that is never brought as ביכורים.
steps.simpleTranslation: But perhaps: just as מרור is from a species that has no ביכורים, so too מצה must be from a species that has no ביכורים!
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא challenges רבי עקיבא's comparison. It suggests the comparison could prove far too much. The answer comes on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: מרור is not only 'not ביכורים'; its whole species is never brought as ביכורים. If the comparison works at the species level, wheat and barley would be invalid for מצה, and only grains like spelt would work. That would be a sweeping result, so the ברייתא will need to explain why it does not follow; the answer comes on the next amud.

keyTerms.meaning: If you say / perhaps (introducing a counter-reading)
In its species, meaning its whole type of plant

phrases.english: If so: just as bitter herbs
whose species has no first fruits,
so too matza whose species has no first fruits!
phrases.notes: That would rule out wheat and barley, leaving grains like spelt.
